title: Inverse of a 2×2
prompt:
Find the inverse:

    [[1, -5], [-5, -1]]

Enter exact fractions.
recap:
For a 2×2 [[a, b], [c, d]] with det = ad − bc ≠ 0, the inverse is (1/det)·[[d, −b], [−c, a]]: swap the diagonal, negate the off-diagonal, divide by the determinant. A·A⁻¹ = I.

Example — A = [[4, 7], [2, 6]]: det = 24 − 14 = 10, so A⁻¹ = (1/10)[[6, −7], [−2, 4]] = [[3/5, −7/10], [−1/5, 2/5]].

Exact fractions avoid rounding. Reference: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, §2.5.
